nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light that reaches the forest floor only in gaps and clearings, so canopy trees and understory plants compete hard for it.

nodes.name: Equatorial rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy, year-round rain keeps the Congo Basin forest wet and feeds the rivers and swamps around the reserve.

nodes.name: Dja River and swamps
nodes.desc: The Dja River loops around almost the whole reserve, forming its natural boundary, and its banks and swamps hold water-loving plants and animals.

nodes.name: Forest soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients released from leaf litter and dead wood are taken up quickly by roots and fungi.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil animals break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs are eaten by monkeys, apes, birds and many other animals, which spread their seeds.

nodes.name: Wild mango trees
nodes.desc: A large-seeded forest tree of the Congo Basin; its fruit is a food for forest animals, and elephants help carry its seeds.

nodes.name: Ebony trees
nodes.desc: A genus of forest trees with fleshy fruit and hard dense wood; Diospyros conocarpa is among the most recorded plants near the reserve.

nodes.name: Marantaceae herbs
nodes.desc: Broad-leaved herbs carpeting forest openings and swampy ground, an important food for gorillas and elephants.

nodes.name: Lianas and understory shrubs
nodes.desc: Woody climbers are common in the reserve forest; their leaves and shoots feed many browsers.

nodes.name: Western lowland gorilla
nodes.desc: Mostly a plant eater; it prefers ripe fruit and turns to leaves, herbs and bark when fruit is scarce, and it spreads seeds.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and many kinds of fruit and carries seeds long distances, which earns it the name megagardener of the forest.

nodes.name: Forest buffalo
nodes.desc: A smaller forest form of the African buffalo that feeds on herbs and grasses in forest clearings and along the swamps.

nodes.name: Blue duiker
nodes.desc: A tiny forest antelope that eats mostly fallen fruit, plus leaves, flowers and some ants.

nodes.name: Greater spot-nosed monkey
nodes.desc: A tree-living guenon recorded near the reserve that eats mainly fruit and is hunted by eagles, leopards and chimpanzees.

nodes.name: Grey-cheeked mangabey
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating canopy monkey on the reserve species list; the white-collared mangabey is also protected there.

nodes.name: Black-casqued hornbill
nodes.desc: A large forest hornbill, the most recorded of the big birds near the reserve, that eats fruit and spreads seeds.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Termites eat dead wood and plant litter and are themselves food for apes, reptiles and other insect eaters.

nodes.name: Chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Eats mostly fruit but also hunts monkeys and small antelopes and fishes for termites with sticks.

nodes.name: Crested chameleon
nodes.desc: A forest chameleon of Cameroon and neighbouring countries that is recorded near the reserve and feeds on small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: The top cat of the reserve; in Central African forests it preys mainly on duikers and primates, and also takes buffalo and sometimes chimpanzees.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A powerful forest eagle that hunts monkeys and small antelopes such as duikers from the canopy.
